description: On termination of a Partner Agreement the Partner stops holding itself out as a Partner, invoices fall due, earned commissions are paid, and customer transition is supported.

approval.ruling: owner, 2026-09-13 as extended 2026-09-18 (C-23) — this standard restates §31.8 without changing its meaning

source_document: Legal Constitution, Lawyer Review Version L1.10 — docs/02-legal-domain/LEGAL_CONSTITUTION_L1.10.md
source_quote: On termination of a Partner Agreement: (a) the Partner must immediately cease identifying itself as a Partner and stop using the Company's trademarks/marketing materials; (b) outstanding invoices for Services provided to the Partner's End Customers become due within 15 days of termination; (c) the Company pays out earned, unpaid commissions for pre-termination referrals, except that commissions may be forfeited (with stated reasoning) if termination was for the Partner's fraud or illegal conduct; (d) the Partner cooperates with a Company-requested End Customer transition, capped at 30 days, during which the Company will not disrupt End Customer service provided fees are paid; (e) Confidential Information is returned/destroyed per Section 15.

evaluation_rules._note: presence is established by the mapping layer alone (45D)

aliases: cease identifying itself as a partner

_calibration: ONE COMPOUND PRESENCE REQUIREMENT, NOT FIVE — the `AM-66` precedent: service discontinuation is one compound PRESENCE requirement and never the notice limb alone. §31.8's (a)-(e) are the consequences of a single event and are evaluated together; splitting them would let a document satisfy (a) and be recorded as meeting §31.8.

§31.8 carries TWO numbers — 15 days for outstanding invoices and a 30-day transition cap — but this standard is PRESENCE, not NUMERIC_COMPARISON. A numeric standard measures ONE basis, and these are two different bases inside one clause; asserting either as THE comparison would misreport the other. If a Partner Agreement is supplied and the numbers need measuring, each gets its own standard (45B).
Limb (e) defers to Section 15, which is already covered by the Confidentiality standards — not restated here.
